scenes.headline: How an RTX card learns to speak Metal
scenes.sub: A Mac graphics driver assembled from open parts
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Lantern! Here is how a modern NVIDIA card ends up running Apple's Metal graphics.

scenes.text: Since Turing, NVIDIA's kernel driver mostly carries messages to firmware on the GPU, so a Mac only needs the glue.
scenes.say: Since the Turing generation, NVIDIA's kernel driver mostly carries messages to firmware running on the card. So the hard part already exists. A Mac only needs the glue.

scenes.title: One draw call, top to bottom

steps.say: A Metal app calls a plugin that subclasses Apple's own private device class, so Metal accepts it as a driver.
Shaders arrive in Apple's bitcode format and are translated into the portable format Vulkan uses.
Mesa's open Vulkan driver compiles them for the card and builds the command buffers.
Its requests travel over the Mac's driver interface to NVIDIA's own kernel code, rebuilt for macOS.
And that code passes nearly everything to firmware on the card's own processor, through shared memory queues.

scenes.title: Convincing macOS
scenes.say: The new work is mostly persuasion.

items.say: A relative path makes Metal load the plugin from outside the sealed system volume.
Apple's kernel accelerator class was rebuilt from its binary, slot by slot.
Any private method the plugin lacks is logged and answered with zeroes.
And Mesa's Linux style requests ride over a fake file descriptor.

scenes.credit: A user's report in the project's issues
scenes.title: Metal 3 on a Turing card

steps.say: On a user's RTX card, System Information reports Metal support as Metal three.
On a PC presenting itself as an iMac Pro.

scenes.label: in the device table, one card physically validated
scenes.say: The installer lists two hundred thirty five cards. One was physically validated. Mesh shaders are emulated, and ray tracing runs in software.

scenes.text: The chip knowledge lives in NVIDIA's firmware and Mesa's driver; the new work is the glue macOS accepts.
scenes.say: The knowledge of the chip lives in NVIDIA's firmware and Mesa's driver. What is new is the glue that macOS accepts.

recap: A plugin that poses as Apple's driver
Shaders translated, then Mesa's Vulkan driver
NVIDIA's kernel code talking to firmware
scenes.say: A plugin posing as Apple's driver. Translated shaders on Mesa's Vulkan driver. And NVIDIA's own code, talking to its firmware.
